skill.name: verging-ai-tts
skill.description: Convert text to speech audio using OpenAI TTS-1-HD through the verging.ai proxy API. Supports multiple voices, playback speed control, and various audio output formats.
skill.summary: Generate text-to-speech audio through the verging.ai proxy API with OpenAI TTS-1-HD voices.
skill.author: verging-ai

security_audit.summary: The skill documents a verging.ai text-to-speech API workflow. The real risks are expected external network transmission of user text and generated audio URLs; the command-execution and system-reconnaissance matches are Markdown false positives.

remediation.suggestion: Document that input text is sent to verging.ai and should not include confidential data without user approval.

remediation.issue: Generated audio is returned as an external URL
remediation.suggestion: Clarify retention, access controls, and sharing expectations for generated CDN audio links.

remediation.issue: API key examples appear in setup instructions
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples as placeholders and advise users to store real keys in a secret manager or environment variable.

content.value_statement: Producing natural narration from text usually requires separate TTS tooling and API setup. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through verging.ai TTS requests with voice and speed options.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to authenticate with a verging.ai API key.
Documents the POST endpoint for verging.ai text-to-speech requests.
Lists supported voices: alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, and shimmer.
Describes speed control from 0.25x to 4.0x and MP3 output.
Shows request and response examples, including audio URL and credit usage.
Summarizes common error codes and credit costs.
limitations: Requires a verging.ai account, API key, and available credits.
Text input is limited to 4096 characters per request.
Generated audio is delivered through an external CDN URL.
It documents API usage; it does not add a local TTS engine.

output_examples.input: Explain what happens when a request is too long.
output_examples.output: The service rejects text over 4096 characters. Split the script into smaller sections and retry each section.

best_practices: Store the verging.ai API key in a secret manager or environment variable.
Review text for confidential data before sending it to an external TTS service.
Choose voice and speed settings that match the audience and content length.
anti_patterns: Pasting real API keys into prompts, chat logs, or examples.
Sending regulated or private text without approval.
Using one long request when shorter segments would improve review and retries.

faq.question: Does this skill generate audio locally?
faq.answer: No. It documents requests to the verging.ai API, which returns generated audio through an external URL.

faq.question: Which voices are documented?
faq.answer: The skill lists alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, and shimmer.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires a verging.ai API key and available credits.

faq.question: What input size is supported?
faq.answer: The documented maximum input size is 4096 characters per request.

faq.question: Can I control playback speed?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents speed values from 0.25x to 4.0x.

faq.question: Is it safe for confidential text?
faq.answer: Treat submitted text as external service data. Use it only when your data policy allows external TTS processing.
